findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. When a pull request author has a login but no display name, `person()` uses the login as `starter["name"]`. The fallback to the item's recorded start-commit name is then skipped. A normally started item with both a known git name and a login shows the login in both fields instead of keeping the name beside it. The command-level login test supplies an author with both fields, so it does not catch this case.
findings.title: Not done: a login-only pull request hides the starter's recorded name

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Scale. This fallback calls `_starters(top)` separately for every row without a loaded pull request author. Although `repo.command_fact` caches the git log text, `_starters` splits and rebuilds the complete starter map on each call. The HTML board uses `trim=False`, so a repo with hundreds of older items outside the pull-request window repeatedly parses its full starter history; the previous code built that map once per board read.
findings.title: Reparsing every starter commit for each historical row slows the HTML board
